title: What is a Context Window?  #aiautomation #techtok
description:
Context window. The term gets thrown around constantly and most people do not actually know what it controls.

A context window is how much text, measured in tokens, your AI model can see at one time. That includes your current prompt, the conversation history, and any background information you gave it earlier.

More context generally means better answers. If you ask an AI for business advice and it knows nothing about your business, the response is generic. If it has pages of context about how your business actually works, the answer becomes specific and useful.

But there are limits. Overload the context window completely and in some cases the model can hard error and crash. More commonly, the model starts deprioritizing older information as new information comes in. Different models handle this differently, but the general pattern is that recent context gets prioritized over older context. So if you gave the model detailed information about your business months ago and it has since scrolled out of the window, asking it a question now will not get you the response you are expecting.

Understanding how your context window fills up and what falls out of it is one of the simplest ways to get dramatically better results.
